overall: The AG found the Wayland School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to cite the confidentiality statute for a Purpose 7 executive session in the notice, chair's announcement, and minutes, though the session itself was permissible and the violation was not intentional.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the executive session topic in the August 28 meeting notice (Purpose 7, compliance with a general law) was insufficient.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee did not identify the statute that required its deliberations be kept confidential, either in the meeting notice or in the announcement in open session.

allegations.summary: Although not separately framed as a claim, the chair's open-session announcement before the Purpose 7 executive session failed to cite the statute requiring confidentiality.
allegations.key_passage: the Committee should have cited to the Public Records Law, both in the meeting notice and in the announcement prior to convening in executive session.

allegations.summary: The AG reviewed the August 28 executive session minutes on its own initiative (not alleged in the complaint) and found the Purpose 7 discussion summary inadequate.
allegations.key_passage: The minutes of the Purpose 7 discussion are wholly insufficient, failing to even identify the topic or specific matter at issue.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
Within 30 days, draft and approve revised minutes of the August 28 executive session that include the missing detail identified in the letter.
Within 30 days, release to the public the Purpose 7 section of the August 28 executive session minutes, unless the attorney-client privilege or a Public Records Law exemption applies.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
